newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Socialists say EU-funded job scheme is racist.
newsitem.headline: Socialists say EU-funded job scheme is racist.

text.p: A European Union-funded job finder scheme appears to allow discrimination against ethnic minorities, the leader of the European Parliament Socialists, Pauline Green, said on Wednesday.

She cited the case of a British citizen of Iranian descent who applied for a job in Belgium advertised through the EU-wide Euris scheme, only to be told that the job description had changed and his previously suitable qualifications were no longer adequate.

"There are racist overtones to the way the job description was changed after he'd applied for the job," Green told a news conference to launch the Socialists' plan of action for the European Year Against Racism and Xenophobia.
Green also attacked the British government for blocking the creation of an EU centre to collect data about racism and xenophobia, saying it was an outrage.
British Home Office minister Timothy Kirkhope said on Monday that London "fully supported" the idea of a European monitoring centre but objected to creating it under the proposed EU treaty provision.
MEPs are due to hold their annual debate on tackling racism on Wednesday afternoon, one day before the European Year Against Racism and Xenophobia is launched in the Hague.
Green said the Socialists wanted to ensure the 12-month campaign produced practical results and not just fine words.
To this end the group will be commissioning leading European academics to conduct research into the difficulties facing immigrants in the EU, as a basis for future policies.
The Socialists are also demanding the insertion in the EU treaty of a new clause outlawing racism, xenophobia and anti- semitism.

Green announced the group planned to create a network of legal advisers to help people with immigration and asylum problems and organise conferences on racism with non-governmental organisations in all 15 EU member states.
